answer: Influence comes from repeated escrowed trades with distinct counterparties, and each partner’s contribution is capped. A new identity has no history, so a comet swarm of aliases cannot gain influence by trading only among itself; a mirror check discounts circular exchanges. To build reputation, the attacker must lock funds and find genuine partners for each alias, paying real capital and time, with escrow at risk if trades fail. The network updates its delta as new behavior appears.
